title: Activation ablation at equal width (one hidden layer, w31)
question: Does the Kerr activation exp(i c |z|^2) z give an advantage over other complex activations at equal width?
git_commit: recorded per run in results/runs/*.json (field git_commit); rule commit: see LOG.md
eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation

activation_notes.kerr_c_train: the current activation: ONE trainable c per layer (NonlinearPhase), not per neuron
activation_notes.kerr_c_fixed: c is a buffer (not trained) = median final c of kerr_c_train runs of the same width, steps (and lr in S1); the *_fixed stages run after the kerr_c_train ones
activation_notes.kerr_taylor1: z + a |z|^2 z with complex a (2 parameters, c_mult applies)
activation_notes.sigmoid_gate: z * sigmoid(a |z|^2 + b), a and b per neuron (b = 2 at start)

c_fixed_fallback_source: median final c1 of E012 v3/v4 one_hidden w31 runs (smoke and estimate only)

rule_draft.status: DRAFT: to be confirmed by the user before the first run; must not change after results are seen
rule_draft.kerr_vs_a: Kerr (kerr_c_train) is better than activation A at equal h if the difference of mean test >= 1 p.p. (~0.035 dB) and the min-max intervals do not overlap; otherwise not distinguishable (S2 per width, S3 at h48)
rule_draft.trainable_c: trainability of c is needed if kerr_c_train - kerr_c_fixed >= 0.5 p.p.
rule_draft.nonlinearity: nonlinearity is needed if the best non-linear activation - identity >= 20 p.p.
rule_draft.rm: RM_total printed: Kerr adds 7h RM (h = 48: 336 of 6 480, ~5 %)
rule_draft.noise: thresholds in p.p. are compared with results/noise_floor.json (E024): MDD(5 seeds) = t_{0.975,8} * s_pooled * sqrt(2/5); 0.1 dB of Q2 = 6 p.p. at 10 %, 4.1 at 48 %, 3.0 at 66 %, 2.7 at 70 % (anchors); every table prints both
